links.outcome: Agreement of automated LM evaluators with physicians in detecting errors in LM-generated medical text
links.effect: MedVAL fine-tuning raised average F1 from 66% to 83% (p < 0.001), with per-sample safety classification scores up to 86%; GPT-4o improved by 8%.
links.quote: MedVAL fine-tuning significantly improves (p < 0.001) alignment with physicians on both seen and unseen tasks, increasing average F1 scores from 66% to 83%, with per-sample safety classification scores up to 86%.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an automated evaluator/guardrail method (MedVAL, an LM-as-judge safety classifier) to detect factual inconsistencies and risk in AI-generated medical outputs, benchmarked against physician annotations.
